original_finding.title: Admin handoff state survives later user handoff and disables managed writer fencing despite R04/R05 being marked complete
original_finding.description: A browser session that carries both `request.session.stcontrolAdmin` and a managed user envelope skips `stcontrolRequestTracker()` fencing because the middleware returns early on the admin marker.

root_cause.summary: The adapter stores admin and user handoff state in two independent session fields and never makes them mutually exclusive. `stcontrolHandoffHandler()` writes `request.session.stcontrolAdmin` for admin handoff and `request.session.stcontrol` for user handoff, but neither branch clears the opposite role. `stcontrolRequestTracker()` then trusts `request.session.stcontrolAdmin` as an unconditional bypass, so any later user write from the same cookie skips stale-writer, lease, quiesce, and data-fault checks.
evidence: src/endpoints/stcontrol.js:441-450 stores `request.session.stcontrolAdmin` for admin handoff and does not clear `request.session.stcontrol` first.
src/endpoints/stcontrol.js:476-478 stores the managed user envelope via `registerStcontrolSession()` and does not clear any existing `request.session.stcontrolAdmin`.
src/stcontrol.js:930-979 returns immediately when `request.session?.stcontrolAdmin` exists, before any stale-session, gate, or lease validation runs.
No existing route or adapter test reuses one cookie across admin->user or user->admin transitions and then exercises a fenced write path.

state_contamination_paths.name: admin_to_user
sequence: Later user handoff stores a managed `request.session.stcontrol` at src/endpoints/stcontrol.js:478 without deleting the admin marker.
Subsequent authenticated writes hit src/stcontrol.js:932 and bypass all managed-user fencing because the admin marker still exists.

state_contamination_paths.name: user_to_admin
sequence: User handoff stores a managed `request.session.stcontrol` envelope at src/stcontrol.js:865-870 and durable session/lease state at src/stcontrol.js:873-893.
Later admin handoff stores `request.session.stcontrolAdmin` at src/endpoints/stcontrol.js:446-450 without retiring the managed user envelope.
The same cookie now carries both role markers, and later user writes still bypass src/stcontrol.js:932 because admin state wins unconditionally.

logout: src/endpoints/users-public.js:219-235 calls `noteStcontrolLogout(request)` and then sets `request.session = null`, so an explicit logout clears both role markers only because the entire cookie-backed session is discarded.

src/stcontrol.js:901-912 tombstones only the current `request.session.stcontrol.sessionId`; it does not independently clear `stcontrolAdmin`, so without the route-level `request.session = null` the mixed-role state would persist.
heartbeat: src/server-main.js:347 mounts `/api/users` public routes before `requireLoginMiddleware` at src/server-main.js:393 and before `setupPrivateEndpoints(app)` installs `stcontrolRequestTracker` at src/server-startup.js:154-161.

src/endpoints/users-public.js:242-268 therefore handles `/api/users/heartbeat` on the public router path. It calls `noteStcontrolPageHeartbeat()` at line 255, but that helper only checks for a durable session tombstone and ignores lease freshness (`src/stcontrol.js:915-927`).

Direct read-only reproduction on August 15, 2026 showed `stcontrolRequestTracker()` returns `409 stale_writer_session` for a stale managed heartbeat request without `stcontrolAdmin`, but the same request continues when the admin marker is present; `noteStcontrolPageHeartbeat()` returns `true` in both cases because it does not validate the lease.

remediation_plan.strategy: Make admin and user handoff state mutually exclusive at the handoff boundary, so the request tracker sees exactly one role for a given browser session. Keep the fix scoped to the handoff/logout edge and add one mixed-cookie regression on the real fenced write path.

steps.change: Before completing a successful user handoff, delete any stale `request.session.stcontrolAdmin` marker so the next authenticated request must pass managed-user fencing.

Before completing a successful admin handoff, retire any existing managed user envelope: call `noteStcontrolLogout(request)` when `request.session.stcontrol?.sessionId` exists, then delete `request.session.stcontrol` before setting `request.session.stcontrolAdmin`.

Add a route regression that reuses one `sharedSession` cookie across admin->user and user->admin handoffs and asserts the session object never retains both `stcontrolAdmin` and `stcontrol` after a successful handoff.

Add a write-path regression that seeds a stale or missing managed lease, reuses the mixed cookie, and proves a POST routed through `stcontrolRequestTracker()` returns `409 stale_writer_session` once handoff mutual exclusion is enforced.

Add one logout boundary assertion proving explicit `/api/users/logout` clears the entire session and tombstones only the exact durable session id. Treat heartbeat ordering as an adjacent follow-up: either document that it is intentionally public and not a lease fence, or move/equate its lease check separately.

remediation_plan.minimal_fix_scope: The minimum patch needed to close act-001 is role-exclusivity during handoff plus two regressions: one mixed-cookie session-shape test and one fenced write test. Heartbeat routing can be tracked separately unless acceptance explicitly requires heartbeat itself to prove lease freshness.

correctness: The finding is real for both admin->user and user->admin cookie reuse. Once `stcontrolAdmin` remains in the session, all later authenticated user writes skip the exact stale-writer and lease checks that R04/R05 rely on.
The issue persists until explicit logout because no successful handoff path clears the opposite role marker.
logout_and_heartbeat_boundary: Logout is the only current cleanup path that definitely removes the contaminated cookie because it nulls the whole session object.
Heartbeat does not mitigate the bug. It does not clear `stcontrolAdmin`, and because it lives on the public router path it should not be treated as evidence that managed lease fencing is active.
existing_test_coverage: tests/stcontrol-adapter.node.test.mjs:347-373 covers stale managed writes without an admin marker and correctly expects `stale_writer_session`.
tests/stcontrol-native-entry-guards.node.test.mjs:81-100 covers which public/native account routes are exposed, but it does not exercise mixed-role session state.
missing_regressions: No existing test reuses one cookie for admin->user or user->admin handoff and then POSTs through `stcontrolRequestTracker()`.
No existing test captures the logout boundary for mixed-role cleanup.
No existing acceptance test documents that `/api/users/heartbeat` is mounted before the private tracker and therefore is not itself a managed-lease fence.

validation_status.details: All 25 baseline tests passed on August 15, 2026. Existing coverage proves the isolated handoff and stale-writer behaviors, but it leaves the mixed-cookie contamination path untested. Read-only inline reproduction also confirmed `stcontrolRequestTracker()` blocks a stale managed heartbeat/write request without `stcontrolAdmin` and allows it to continue when the admin marker is present.

reassessed_severity.justification: The bug is reachable with ordinary browser cookie reuse, invalidates the intended single-writer/session-fence behavior for real user writes, and directly contradicts the acceptance claim that R04/R05 are already closed. It is not merely cosmetic state drift.
